name: TV DIABLO Windows
note: v2184: v2174 created tv/chron_hunt_memory.json, which is live state holding item names lifted off his own reels, and I did not add it to gitignore. Hours later his console was relaunched onto the build that writes it, the file appeared in the working tree, and a git add of everything swept it into a commit that went to a PUBLIC repo. Ten keys of set piece names, so the content is mild, and the outcome is entirely wrong. It is untracked and ignored now, along with the auto relaunch setting file created in v2180 which had the same exposure. tv/chronicle_swept.json has been ignored for exactly this reason since the day it was created, so the rule already existed. What was missing was anything that enforces it on the NEXT file. run_gates already keeps a list of the files the console writes at runtime, and review_lite already blocks a push when a new one is missing from that list. This closes the other half: being on that list must also mean being ignored by git. Two guards, because they answer different questions. One asks whether git WOULD ignore each path, which is about the future and works even when the file is absent on this machine. The other asks whether any of them is tracked RIGHT NOW, because gitignore does nothing for a file already in the index and the console would publish his data on every future run. Both were proven red by re force adding the file back. Remembering is not a mechanism.
